texts.30f0422bd34b: There are three tests commonly used to diagnose bowel problems in patients with symptoms of colorectal cancer: CT colonography (CTC), colonoscopy, and barium enema. The SIGGAR trial is comparing these tests via a randomised controlled trial with respect to: Diagnostic efficacy of CTC, colonoscopy, and barium enema in terms of the number of investigations needed to diagnose or exclude colorectal cancer or large polyps in each diagnostic arm.* Time to diagnosis associated with each investigative pathway.* Psychological and physical morbidity associated with each investigative pathway. Costs of diagnosis associated with each investigative pathway. Frequency, clinical relevance, costs, and psychological and physical morbidity associated with detection of abnormalities outside the colon by CTC. Variability in trained radiologist performance when using CTC. Key: * - aims for which we require data from ONS.
texts.7212ee0948a8: The data supplied by the NHS IC to Cancer Research UK Colorectal Cancer Unit will be used only for the approved Medical Research Project identified above.
